findings.message: Python code imports distutils, lxml, matplotlib, nibabel, nilearn, numpy, pylab, scipy, sklearn but the package has no requirements file, environment file or lockfile. A rerun must choose versions and log them.

Code uses APIs that current releases no longer have: NumPy scalar aliases (np.int, np.float, ...) (removed in NumPy 1.24); nibabel get_data() (removed in nibabel 5.0); nibabel get_affine() / get_header() (deprecated, removed in later nibabel); sklearn.cross_validation (removed in scikit-learn 0.20); sklearn.externals.joblib / six (removed in scikit-learn 0.23); sklearn.datasets.base (removed in scikit-learn 0.24); distutils (removed from the standard library in Python 3.12). Nothing pins versions old enough, so a rerun must either reconstruct an old environment or edit the code, and log which.

Code fetches data over the network when it runs (fetch_adhd, fetch_haxby, fetch_haxby_simple, fetch_miyawaki2008, urlopen). What the server returns today may differ from what the authors got; a receipt must record each file fetched and its SHA-256.
6 scripts, no master script, and the README does not name an order. A rerun must choose one and log it.

Files the code both writes and reads are already in the package: miyawaki/lr_coef.npy, miyawaki/lr_scores.npy, miyawaki/svc_coef.npy, miyawaki/svc_scores.npy, miyawaki/svcl2_scores.npy. A run may read these instead of recomputing them. A receipt must say whether it replayed them or recomputed them, and a matching output hash alone does not show recomputation.
13 other links could not be reached from this machine (DNS, refused, timeout or proxy). That may be this machine's network rather than the link.
No licence file and no licence named in the documentation. Running it for a check is unaffected, but a receipt should quote and hash files rather than redistribute them.
